prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which made possible incretin-based therapy of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part B020 prize to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The round-1 exchange did not weaken the science, and all six of us now name the same trio, so the useful work in this round is to test what that trio rests on rather than to count it. The discovery chain is proglucagon processing, the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, human incretin physiology and receptor biology, then a drug class with large randomized-trial benefit in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal outcomes. It has been independently confirmed for well over a decade, so maturity is not in question. Each credited name has a distinct step: Holst for human physiology and secretion, Mojsov for identification and synthesis of the active peptide, Drucker for receptor biology, GLP-2 and translation. I think a one-achievement prize is the most coherent use of three names. A second part would force a cut to the B020 trio that I could not defend on the record.
statement.case_against: Credit remains the weak point and I do not think the supplied record resolves it. Habener lies outside the credited names, and I cannot adjudicate his priority against Mojsov's from the material we have. Knudsen's long-acting analogue work is what reached patients, so a discovery-centred citation can be read as honouring the idea over the drug. I accept that criticism and judge it the lesser cost, because the prize has generally recognised the enabling discovery, but it is a judgment and not a demonstration. Long-term safety and durability of the obesity indication are still accumulating. Finally, if colleagues conclude the achievement is the therapy itself, my trio is less defensible and Knudsen would have to replace someone.

responses.point: Sandberg moved from Drucker, Holst and Knudsen to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, yet still doubts that a single-achievement prize is the best use of the committee's range and sees B045 and B040 as strong enough for a shared prize.
responses.response: I respect that you moved on attribution, and I agree Knudsen's cost is real. On a two-part prize I come out differently. Any second part has to be paid for from the three-person cap, which means dropping Holst, Mojsov or Drucker from B020, and each of them owns a step that cannot be replaced. B045 would then need three of its six names, and I do not think that reduction is defensible, since Bamberg, Nagel, Hegemann, Boyden, Deisseroth and Miesenbock each have a strong claim. I would sooner leave a field for a later year than split it unfairly this year. My view could change only if someone shows a B020 name is less essential than I think, and I have not seen that argued.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius stresses that unanimous support is not a measure of merit, that attribution must be tested as hard as the science, and that long-term safety of the obesity indication is still being defined.
responses.response: I agree, and I will go slightly further on the chair's own question about wording. The citation should avoid language that assigns first identification of the active peptide, since the Mojsov and Habener question is not settled on this record. Saying 'its active form' honours the contribution without ruling on priority. On safety, the registered benefit in glycaemia, weight and cardiovascular and renal outcomes comes from randomized trials, and the open questions concern very long-term use and the obesity indication. I do not think they bear on whether the discovery occurred. They are not grounds for delay, but I would keep the citation to discovery and the therapy it enabled, with no claim about how long benefit lasts. If you believe the safety data should change timing, I would like to hear which finding you have in mind.

responses.point: Perlmann ranks the unfolded protein response (B052) as a fallback, notes that the cap would force a cut to the B020 trio for any joint prize, and says the case weakens if the Mojsov question cannot be settled.
responses.response: I agree on the cap and on B052's strengths, the clean Mori and Walter pairing above all. Where I would resist is the suggestion that an unsettled Mojsov question weakens B020 enough to change the ordering. Even if Habener's claim were found equal, the likely remedy is a different identity for the peptide-identification slot, not a different prize, because the step itself is needed. B052's clinical consequence is still largely prospective, which is why I place it below B020 this year, not because the science is lacking. As before, I note our shared publication record on dopamine neurons, which does not touch any shortlisted ballot.

responses.point: Linnarsson favours the narrower B040 pairing of June and Sadelain, doubting Rosenberg's contribution to the decisive CAR work and noting Eshhar's omission.
responses.response: I accept your narrower pairing as the better B040 version, and I have moved toward it from my opening trio that included Rosenberg: his strongest work is adoptive cell transfer, not CAR design. Eshhar's absence is still a weakness that I cannot repair from the supplied names. That is why B040 stays an alternative for me and does not become the lead.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's identification of the active peptide stands against Habener's claim cannot be settled from the supplied record, so the citation should not assign priority.
Whether the committee should honour discovery and physiology only, or also drug development, in which case Knudsen would have to replace Mojsov or Drucker.
Whether long-term safety and durability of the obesity indication will change how the achievement is viewed.
Whether CAR-T can be allocated fairly without Eshhar, and whether any of the six optogenetics names can be omitted fairly.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted ballot is apparent from my profile, so I claim no recusal. I disclose that I have co-authored roughly twenty works with Thomas Perlmann on dopamine neurons and related topics, none concerning a shortlisted candidate, and that I worked with Paul Greengard, who is not a candidate. Wahren-Herlenius's field proximity to B034 and El-Manira's to B045 matter only if those ballots advance, and I record no change to my own disclosure since round 1.
